species.habitat_description: Native montane rain and cloud forest on steep wet slopes, using the upper canopy.
species.geographic_description: Endemic to Anjouan and Mohéli in the Comoros.
species.shape_description: Large flying fox with rounded ears, dark wings, and a wingspan up to 1.4 m.
species.behavior_2: Forages in the upper canopy and flies with slow flapping and soaring.
species.life_description_1: Produces one offspring annually, commonly in early September.
species.life_description_2: Captive weaning may take up to eight months.
species.key_fact_1: Endemic to two islands in the Comoros.
species.key_fact_2: Has a wingspan up to 1.4 m despite a body mass near 0.6 kg.
species.key_fact_3: Active during both day and night.
species.threats: Forest conversion for farming, fuel, and construction, plus erosion and landslides.

profile.habitat_note: Upper canopy of steep, wet montane rain and cloud forest.
profile.morphology_note: Blackish flying fox with rounded ears, dark wings, and a wingspan up to 1.4 metres.
profile.diet_note: Eats fruit, flowers, and nectar and disperses pollen and seeds.
profile.behavior_note: Cathemeral social roosting bat that forages in the upper canopy.
profile.reproduction_note: One offspring annually, with captive weaning taking up to eight months.
profile.reference_summary: Two-island Comoros endemic threatened mainly by forest conversion.
